Solve P(trigger) = target in one free parameter

Source: R/ahr_analytic.R
ahr_solve.Rd

Scans f over a grid of the free parameter, brackets every crossing of target, and refines each with stats::uniroot(): the pattern of the mrct-consistency boundary and regional-entry scripts. f maps the free parameter to the probability (typically ahr_design(...)$prob[["p_trigger"]]); when the parameter enters the build (the region prognostic log-HR r, the entry delay), f builds its own population. Roots are only found where the scan brackets them: two crossings between adjacent scan points are missed.

Usage

ahr_solve(f, target, interval, ..., n_scan = 25L, scan = NULL, tol = 1e-08)

Arguments

f

Function of the free parameter (first argument) returning one number.

target

The value to solve for.

interval

Length-2 range of the free parameter.

...

Further arguments passed to f.

n_scan

Number of equally spaced scan points on interval (default 25); ignored when scan is given.

scan

Optional explicit scan points (sorted, within interval).

tol

Tolerance of stats::uniroot() in the free parameter.

Value

A list: roots (sorted), n_roots, values (f at the roots), scan (a data.frame of the scan points x and value), and evaluations (calls to f).

See also

ahr_design()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f <- function(a) ahr_design(ahr_population(dgm, 40, 11,
  entry_delay = list(var = "z_region", delay = a)), 0.55, 2, 1000)$prob[["p_trigger"]]
ahr_solve(f, 0.25, c(0, 24), scan = 0:24)
} # }
